title: Warehouse worker (four days on, four off, 6 AM shifts, not a student) books a Thanksgiving flight to his mother's, back Monday night; the late landing leaves about five hours of sleep before Tuesday's 6 AM shift, and Dev names it once with the choices.

dev_must_notice.what: He booked a flight to Boston, out Fri Nov 27 at 6:10 AM and back Mon Nov 30, leaving at 8:55 PM and landing 10:55 PM (x-flight-east, x-flight-east.return). Two nights get short. Thursday is Thanksgiving and his last shift of the run ends 4:30 PM (shift-main-2026-11-26), then his usual 6 PM gym; with the airport 40 minutes away he is up about 3 AM, so a bed time of 11 PM gives 4 hours. Monday he lands at 10:55 PM, is home around 12:20 AM, and the next run starts Tue Dec 1 at 6 AM (shift-main-2026-12-01), up at 5:00, so he sleeps about 4 hours 40 minutes. Both nights are fixable only before they happen. Nothing else collides: the weekend is days off, and the Saturday gym is not needed in Boston.

best_fix.what: Thursday 8:00 PM, after the gym and dinner: 'Flight is at 6:10, so you're up around 3. Bed by 8:30 gives you about 6 hours. Want it?' with [Remind me at 8:15] [Not tonight]. Dev sets nothing without the tap and gives no gym advice.
best_fix.why: The gym stays at 6 PM (his usual window) and the evening still has two hours at home before a bed time that works. The reminder only helps if he wants it.

best_fix.what: One line after he booked: 'Heads up, Monday's flight lands at 10:55 PM and your next run starts at 6 AM, about 4 hours 40 minutes of sleep. Want me to look at an earlier flight home on Monday, or keep this one?' with [Look at earlier flights] [Keep it]. Dev shows options and prices from the airline's own site and rebooks nothing.
best_fix.why: The choice is his and it costs money to change, so Dev asks once and offers to look; keeping the flight is fine and Dev drops it.

must_not: book a Saturday 6 PM workout while he is in Boston
tell him the Thursday gym should be skipped, or move his Thursday gym
rebook, cancel or change the flight, or tell him a flight is better without showing it
count the paycheck or the first run's pay as money he has for the trip
use guilt words about the trip, the booking or sleep
remind him of the weekly grocery run on Wed Nov 25 as a problem, or call the missed Saturday gym a miss
assumptions: His rotation is 4 days on, 4 off from the persona (Nov 23 to 26 on, Nov 27 to 30 off, Dec 1 to 4 on); Thanksgiving Thursday is a regular shift, not a holiday day off.
Home and Boston are both in the persona's time zone; the flights are 3 hours 15 minutes out and 2 hours back as the case states them (a made-up route).
Leaving for the airport about 3:30 AM puts him up at about 3 AM; Monday's landing is 10:55 PM with the airport 40 minutes away, and the simulator's timeline puts him at home 12:20 AM.
Money is not part of this case: checking is $3,817.25 and the Dec 1 rent is $1,464.77.

tempting.suggestion: book a Saturday 6 PM workout while he is in Boston
tempting.why_wrong: he is away Fri to Mon; his Tue, Thu and Sat 6 PM gym (m-01) does not apply on the trip and Dev must not count it as missed
